turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good morning. Kindly have a seat, I will check your vitals before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, sister. I have been sitting in the waiting area, so it should be a resting reading.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one twenty-eight over seventy-eight. Pulse is ninety-six. Oxygen saturation is ninety-eight percent. Temperature is thirty-six point eight Celsius.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen has frozen again. One second. Right, it moved. What brings you in?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I am having palpitations, and some breathlessness along with it. It has been going on for the past—
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): About three weeks, doctor. He keeps telling everyone it is nothing much.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): The cursor jumped, sorry. Palpitations and shortness of breath for three weeks? Please say that once more.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. For three weeks my heart races and I feel short of breath. It is worse at night, and it also comes before my exams and before meetings at work.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is there any chest pain with it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. There is no chest pain.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fainting, or a sense that you might black out?
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last Tuesday at college he suddenly had to sit in the corridor because he—
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It was not a blackout, doctor. I sat down and it eased in a few minutes. I did not lose consciousness.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): I was typing, I only heard the end. What happened on Tuesday, again?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): The heart was racing and I was breathless, so I sat on a bench. It settled after a few minutes. There was no fainting.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much coffee are you having?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Four or five cups a day, doctor. I also take energy drinks when I study late.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Some days it is more. Yesterday, before the mock test, he had two cans of Monster, plus the coffee.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not smoke cigarettes, doctor. I do vape, a few times in the evening.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Since when have you been vaping?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): For about eight months.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He will say stress is not a problem, but before every exam he paces the flat the whole night. I am his partner, I live with him, so I see it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): With due respect, I would not call it stress, doctor. I am managing. It is only the schedule.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines that you take?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing on a regular basis, doctor. My mother had given an Ayurvedic powder, but I never—
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He did not take that powder at all. Only Gelusil, when the coffee brings on acidity.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Gelusil, how often? Please repeat, a pop-up covered the note.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Two or three times in a week, one tablet, only when there is acidity. Not every day.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have no allergies that I know of.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history of heart disease, or thyroid problems?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): My father has high blood pressure. There has been no heart attack in the family.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Alcohol, well, actually I—
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry to cut in, but that cricket last night was something else. The captain's cover drive in the final over, I think the whole building heard me.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): I only saw the highlights while this machine was booting. That six over long-on, and then the run-out, quite unbelievable.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the weather on the way, we got properly soaked near the metro. Typical Bangalore rain, no warning.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, it was pouring. Sorry, doctor, to come back to your question, I do not take alcohol.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, ECG has a free slot at eleven fifteen, shall I hold it?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, please book the ECG. I am ordering thyroid tests as well, TSH and free T4.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): May I ask if this is something serious? My semester exams begin next Monday, and I have a client meeting on Wednesday.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): I cannot say for certain today. These palpitations may be from the coffee, the energy drinks and the vaping, but a thyroid problem or a rhythm disturbance is still possible, so we need the tests.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): I have listened. The chest is clear, there is no wheeze, and the heart sounds are normal. The pulse is fast, about a hundred a minute.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He wakes out of sleep with it too. He has not said how often.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): That is correct, doctor. On two or three nights a week I wake up with the heart racing and a little breathlessness.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Weight loss? Loose motions?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, and no weight loss. My motions are normal, doctor.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Until the reports are back, stop the energy drinks completely, cut coffee to one cup a day, and stop the vaping. If the palpitation starts, breathe in for four counts and out for six. Please practise that twice a day also, not only in the moment.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I will follow your advice, doctor. Giving up the vape before meetings will be difficult, but I will try.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Shall we come back once the reports are there?
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Come for a review in two or three days, when the ECG and the thyroid results are ready. Please ask reception to book it on the way out.

spec.situation: Young adult with palpitations and breathlessness, worse at night and before exams or work meetings; downplays stress, drinks a lot of coffee and energy drinks, vapes; friend or partner contributes. Doctor orders ECG and thyroid tests, discusses breathing exercises.
features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Negative family history of thyroid problems was asked about and not recorded; the patient said only that his father has high blood pressure and there has been no heart attack in the family, leaving no documented thyroid family history answer.
The patient denied loss of consciousness/blackout specifically: on Tuesday he had to sit down during palpitations and breathlessness, it eased within a few minutes, and he did not lose consciousness.
The patient reported waking from sleep with palpitations and a little breathlessness on two or three nights a week; the shortness-of-breath symptom entry is missing this nocturnal frequency/detail.
The patient said he had been sitting in the waiting area so the vital signs should be a resting reading.
The patient stated he does not take any regular medicines and did not take the Ayurvedic powder his mother had given him.
The follow-up plan included asking reception to book the review appointment on the way out.
